questions.question: How many tonnes of gold have been mined in all of human history, as of the end of 2025?
questions.explainer: Roughly 220,000 tonnes of gold have ever been mined, which would form a cube only about 22 metres on each side, and about two-thirds of it was dug up after 1950.
questions.source_title: How much gold has been mined? - World Gold Council

questions.question: How many years ago did Ötzi the Iceman, found frozen in the Alps in 1991, die?
questions.explainer: Ötzi lived between about 3350 and 3105 BC, roughly 5,300 years ago, centuries before the Great Pyramid or Stonehenge's sarsen circle. He still had an arrowhead in his shoulder.

questions.question: How much will the ITER tokamak fusion machine being built in France weigh when complete, in tonnes?
questions.explainer: The ITER tokamak will weigh 23,000 tonnes, about three times the mass of the Eiffel Tower, with its vacuum vessel alone accounting for roughly 5,000 tonnes.

questions.question: How many international migrants (people living outside the country they were born in) were there worldwide in 2024?
questions.explainer: Migrants are about 3.7% of humanity; if they formed one country it would be the fourth most populous on Earth.

questions.question: What is the total area of Greenland, the world's largest island?
questions.explainer: Greenland is about three times the size of Texas, but roughly 80% of it is buried under an ice sheet up to 3 km thick.

questions.question: At what temperature in degrees Celsius does tungsten, the metal with the highest melting point, melt?
questions.explainer: Tungsten melts at 3,422 °C, more than three times the melting point of gold (1,064 °C), which is why it was the filament of choice in incandescent bulbs for a century.

questions.question: What was the average price of a Big Mac in the United States in July 2024, according to The Economist's Big Mac index?
questions.explainer: The Economist has tracked burger prices since 1986 as a light-hearted guide to currency values. The US Big Mac passed $6 in 2025.
questions.source_title: The Economist - Big Mac index data (big-mac-raw-index.csv, USA, 2024-07-01)

questions.question: How many Concorde supersonic airliners were built in total, including prototypes?
questions.explainer: Just 20 Concordes were built: two prototypes, two pre-production aircraft and 16 production models, 14 of which flew passengers for British Airways and Air France.

questions.question: How many minutes did Yuri Gagarin's 1961 spaceflight last, from launch to landing?
questions.explainer: The first human spaceflight was a single orbit of Earth lasting about 108 minutes, shorter than most feature films.

questions.question: How many stone blocks are estimated to make up the Great Pyramid of Giza?
questions.explainer: Roughly 2.3 million blocks averaging over two tonnes each were laid in about 20 years, which works out to a block set every few minutes, day and night. It was the tallest structure on Earth for 3,800 years.

questions.question: What was Luxembourg's GDP per person in 2023, in current US dollars (World Bank)?
questions.explainer: The highest of any country. The figure is inflated because over 200,000 cross-border commuters add to GDP but not to the resident population of about 670,000.
questions.source_title: FRED / World Bank - Gross Domestic Product Per Capita for Luxembourg (PCAGDPLUA646NWDB)

questions.question: How many metres below sea level is the surface of the Dead Sea, as of 2025?
questions.explainer: The Dead Sea's shores are the lowest land on Earth, and the lake is still dropping by more than a metre a year as the Jordan River's inflow is diverted upstream.

questions.question: How many people worldwide were living with HIV at the end of 2023?
questions.explainer: About 1.3 million people were newly infected and 630,000 died of AIDS-related illnesses that year, while roughly 77% of people with HIV were on treatment.
questions.source_title: Global HIV & AIDS statistics — Fact sheet (UNAIDS)

questions.question: How many copies of the Harry Potter books had been sold worldwide as of 2023?
questions.explainer: More than 600 million Harry Potter books have been sold in over 80 languages, the best-selling book series ever: enough for one copy for every 13 people alive.

questions.question: How much prize money did FIFA pay Argentina for winning the 2022 World Cup, in US$?
questions.explainer: Taken from a total prize pot of US$440 million. Even teams knocked out in the group stage collected US$9 million each.
questions.source_title: 2022 World Cup Prize Money (Associated Press via WTOP)

questions.question: How many Scoville heat units does Pepper X, certified the world's hottest chili pepper by Guinness in 2023, average?
questions.explainer: That is several hundred times hotter than a jalapeño (2,500-8,000 SHU) and in the same league as police pepper spray.
questions.source_title: Guinness World Records - Hottest chili pepper

questions.question: How many living languages are spoken in Papua New Guinea?
questions.explainer: With only about 10 million people, Papua New Guinea has more languages than any other country, more than one in every nine languages on Earth.

questions.question: How many words are in Tolstoy's War and Peace in English translation?
questions.explainer: At about 587,000 words, War and Peace is roughly six typical novels in one. A reader managing 250 words a minute would need about 39 hours.

questions.question: How much did James Cameron's Avatar (2009) gross at the worldwide box office, including re-releases?
questions.explainer: Avatar's US$2.92 billion makes it the highest-grossing film ever. Avengers: Endgame briefly took the crown in 2019 until a 2021 re-release in China put Avatar back on top.

questions.question: How many tonnes of crude steel were produced worldwide in 2024?
questions.explainer: The world made 1.88 billion tonnes of steel in 2024, over half of it in China, which is about 230 kg for every person on Earth.
questions.source_title: December 2024 crude steel production and 2024 global totals - worldsteel

questions.question: How many characters are encoded in version 16.0 of the Unicode Standard, released in September 2024?
questions.explainer: Unicode 16.0 added 5,185 characters, including 3,995 Egyptian hieroglyphs; emoji make up fewer than 4,000 of the total, while CJK ideographs account for nearly 100,000.
questions.source_title: Announcing The Unicode Standard, Version 16.0 (Unicode Blog)

questions.question: How many on-demand audio streams were played worldwide in 2024 across all music streaming services (Luminate)?
questions.explainer: Luminate counted about 4.8 trillion on-demand audio streams in 2024: roughly 13 billion a day, or about 600 streams for every person on Earth.

questions.question: How many islands does Sweden have, by Statistics Sweden's official 2013 count?
questions.explainer: Sweden has more islands than any other country, though only about 1,000 are inhabited. Norway (239,057) and Finland (178,947) are next on the list.
questions.source_title: List of islands of Sweden - Wikipedia

questions.question: How many trees are there on Earth, according to the 2015 global estimate published in Nature?
questions.explainer: About 3.04 trillion, roughly 400 trees per person, though the total has fallen by around 46% since the dawn of agriculture.
questions.source_title: Mapping tree density at a global scale - Nature (Crowther et al. 2015)

questions.question: How many runways does Chicago O'Hare International Airport have, as of 2024?
questions.explainer: After a 2021 expansion O'Hare has eight runways, six of them parallel east-west, which helps make it one of the world's busiest airfields by takeoffs and landings.

questions.question: How many hours did Randy Gardner stay awake in his record-setting 1964 sleep-deprivation experiment?
questions.explainer: That is 11 days and 25 minutes without sleep, done as a high-school science project. Guinness no longer tracks the record because of the health risks.

questions.question: What was the population of Greenland on 1 January 2024?
questions.explainer: The world's largest island has fewer residents than a mid-sized town; about a third of them live in the capital, Nuuk, and the population slipped to 56,542 a year later.

questions.question: How many episodes of The Simpsons had aired by the end of season 36 in May 2025?
questions.explainer: Watching all 790 episodes back to back would take about 12 days. The show has averaged roughly 22 episodes a year since it began in 1989.
questions.source_title: List of The Simpsons episodes - Wikipedia

questions.question: What price per seat did Virgin Galactic set when it reopened spaceflight ticket sales in August 2021?
questions.explainer: The 2021 price of $450,000 bought a few minutes of weightlessness on a suborbital hop; earlier deposits had been taken at $200,000 to $250,000 a seat.
questions.source_title: Virgin Galactic is selling tickets to space again, now for $450,000 per seat (Space.com)

questions.question: How much damage did Hurricane Katrina cause in 2005, in 2005 dollars (NOAA estimate)?
questions.explainer: Katrina remains the costliest hurricane in US history; adjusted for inflation the bill is over US$200 billion. Hurricane Harvey in 2017 came closest.

questions.question: How many people died of drug overdoses in the United States in 2023?
questions.explainer: That is nearly 290 people a day, with most deaths involving synthetic opioids such as fentanyl. It was a drop of nearly 3% from 2022, the first annual decline since 2018.
questions.source_title: Drug Overdose Deaths in the United States, 2003–2023 (CDC NCHS Data Brief No. 522)

questions.question: How many different items does the average US supermarket carry, as of 2023?
questions.explainer: The average store stocks almost 32,000 distinct products, yet a typical weekly shop touches only a few dozen of them.
questions.source_title: FMI - The Food Industry Association: Supermarket Facts

questions.question: How much did the United States spend on health care in total in 2023?
questions.explainer: That is about $14,570 per person and 17.6% of US GDP, far more per head than any other country spends.
questions.source_title: NHE Fact Sheet (Centers for Medicare & Medicaid Services)

questions.question: How much was spent on food in the United States in 2023, at home and away from home combined, in US dollars (USDA ERS)?
questions.explainer: More than half of it went to food away from home, meaning restaurants, takeaway and cafeterias, rather than groceries; that is roughly US$7,700 per American.
questions.source_title: USDA Economic Research Service - Food Prices and Spending

questions.question: How many ships transited the Suez Canal in 2023?
questions.explainer: A record 26,434 ships, about 72 a day, used the canal in 2023, before attacks on shipping in the Red Sea diverted much of the traffic around Africa in 2024.

questions.question: How many vacuum tubes did ENIAC, the first general-purpose electronic computer, contain when completed in 1945?
questions.explainer: Several tubes burned out almost every day, and the 27-tonne machine also held about 7,200 diodes, 70,000 resistors, 10,000 capacitors and around 5 million hand-soldered joints.

questions.question: How many Space Shuttle missions did NASA fly between 1981 and 2011?
questions.explainer: Five orbiters flew 135 missions over 30 years, from STS-1 to STS-135, carrying 355 different people and logging more than 1,300 days in space.

questions.question: How many Allied troops landed on the Normandy beaches on D-Day, 6 June 1944?
questions.explainer: About 156,000 American, British and Canadian troops came ashore on the first day, backed by nearly 7,000 ships and more than 11,000 aircraft. It remains the largest seaborne invasion in history.

questions.question: How long is the 2Africa subsea internet cable system, which encircles the African continent?
questions.explainer: That is longer than the circumference of the Earth (40,075 km); the Meta-led cable has 46 landings in 33 countries across Africa, Europe and Asia and is the longest subsea cable system ever built.

questions.question: How much does an Oscar statuette weigh?
questions.explainer: The Academy says the gold-plated bronze figure stands 13.5 inches (34 cm) tall and weighs 8.5 pounds, roughly the weight of a newborn baby.
questions.source_title: Oscar Statuette - Academy of Motion Picture Arts and Sciences

questions.question: How many vending machines are there in Japan, as of the end of 2023?
questions.explainer: Roughly one machine for every 32 people - the highest density in the world. More than half of them sell drinks.
questions.source_title: Japan Vending Machine Manufacturers Association: Number of Vending Machines

questions.question: How much money did migrants send home in remittances to low- and middle-income countries in 2023?
questions.explainer: Remittances now exceed foreign direct investment and official aid to developing countries; India alone received about US$120 billion.
questions.source_title: World Bank – Remittances Slowed in 2023, Expected to Grow Faster in 2024

questions.question: How much does the Rosetta Stone in the British Museum weigh?
questions.explainer: The granodiorite slab is about 112 cm tall, 76 cm wide and 28 cm thick and weighs around 760 kg, roughly the weight of a small car. Its three-script decree from 196 BC unlocked Egyptian hieroglyphs.

questions.question: How long was the complete route of the 2024 Tour de France, in km?
questions.explainer: 21 stages over 23 days, averaging about 167 km a day. That is close to 90% of the straight-line distance from New York to Los Angeles.

questions.question: How many km of high-speed railway did China have in operation at the end of 2024?
questions.explainer: China's high-speed network reached about 48,000 km by the end of 2024, well over half of all high-speed track in the world and longer than the Equator.

questions.question: How many tonnes did the world's wild-capture fisheries land in 2022, per FAO's State of World Fisheries report?
questions.explainer: About 92 million tonnes, and for the first time farmed seafood (aquaculture) now outproduces the wild catch.
questions.source_title: The State of World Fisheries and Aquaculture 2024 - FAO

questions.question: What is the total mass of Earth's atmosphere?
questions.explainer: Sea-level pressure means about 10 tonnes of air press down on every square metre; multiply by Earth's 510 million km² surface and you get roughly 5 quadrillion tonnes, a millionth of Earth's mass.

questions.question: How many people worldwide spoke English as a first or second language in 2024?
questions.explainer: Only about 380 million of them are native speakers; the rest learned English as an additional language, which is why it edges out Mandarin as the most spoken language overall.
questions.source_title: Ethnologue – What are the top 200 most spoken languages?

questions.question: How many cases of wild poliovirus were reported worldwide in 2023?
questions.explainer: All 12 cases were in Afghanistan and Pakistan, the last two countries where wild polio still circulates. In 1988 there were an estimated 350,000 cases a year.
questions.source_title: Progress Toward Poliomyelitis Eradication — Worldwide, January 2022–December 2023 (CDC MMWR)

questions.question: How many confirmed exoplanets were listed in the NASA Exoplanet Archive in September 2025?
questions.explainer: The count passed 5,000 in March 2022 and 6,000 in September 2025, with more than 8,000 further candidates awaiting confirmation.
questions.source_title: The NASA Exoplanet Archive Hits 6,000 Planets (IPAC, Caltech)

questions.question: What is the closest possible distance between Earth and Mars, in kilometres?
questions.explainer: The theoretical minimum is 54.6 million km; the closest recorded approach was 55.7 million km in 2003, and at their farthest the planets are 400 million km apart.
questions.source_title: Go Outside and See Mars! (NASA Watch the Skies blog)

questions.question: How many steps do runners climb in the Empire State Building Run-Up, from the lobby to the 86th-floor observatory?
questions.explainer: That is about 18 steps per floor. The fastest runners climb all 86 floors in roughly 10 minutes.

questions.question: How many households were there in the United States in 2023?
questions.explainer: With about 335 million residents, that works out to roughly 2.5 people per household. Nearly 29% of households are one person living alone.
questions.source_title: U.S. Census Bureau: America's Families and Living Arrangements: 2023 (Table H1)

questions.question: How many yellow taxi medallions (licences to operate a cab) exist in New York City, as of 2024?
questions.explainer: The 1937 Haas Act first froze the number at 13,500, and the count has stood at 13,587 since 2016. At the 2014 peak a single medallion sold for over US$1 million; prices later collapsed to under $200,000.
questions.source_title: Wikipedia: Taxis of New York City

questions.question: What is the surface area of the Pacific Ocean?
questions.explainer: The Pacific covers about 46% of Earth's water surface and nearly a third of the whole planet, more than all of Earth's land area combined.

questions.question: What was the price of the Motorola DynaTAC 8000X, the first commercial handheld mobile phone, when it went on sale in 1984?
questions.explainer: About US$12,000 in today's money for a 'brick' that offered around 30 minutes of talk time and took roughly 10 hours to recharge.

questions.question: How many articles did the English-language Wikipedia have as of mid-2025?
questions.explainer: The 7 millionth article, created on 24 May 2025, was about a 1958 memoir called 'Operators and Things'; English is the largest of more than 300 language editions.

questions.question: How many US dollars did the United States pay France for the Louisiana Purchase in 1803?
questions.explainer: For $15 million the US gained about 828,000 square miles, doubling its size at under 3 cents an acre. Napoleon used the money to fund his wars in Europe.

questions.question: How high above the river is the deck of China's Huajiang Grand Canyon Bridge, the world's highest bridge, opened in 2025, in metres?
questions.explainer: Opened in September 2025 in Guizhou province, its deck hangs 625 m above the Beipan River, nearly twice the height of the Eiffel Tower.

questions.question: What was the United Nations' approved regular budget for the year 2024?
questions.explainer: About 45 cents per person on Earth, and less than New York City spends in two weeks. Peacekeeping is funded separately at roughly $6 billion a year.
questions.source_title: IISD SDG Knowledge Hub - Member States Approve USD 3.59 Billion UN Budget for 2024

questions.question: How old was Jonathan, the Seychelles giant tortoise on St Helena and the oldest known living land animal, in 2025?
questions.explainer: Jonathan is believed to have hatched around 1832, before the first photograph of a person was ever taken, and he is still grazing on the governor's lawn.

questions.question: What is the official seating capacity of Michigan Stadium ('The Big House') in Ann Arbor?
questions.explainer: The largest stadium in the Western Hemisphere. It has squeezed in more than 115,000 people for a 2013 game against Notre Dame.

questions.question: How many golf courses were there worldwide according to the R&A's 2019 'Golf Around the World' report?
questions.explainer: Spread across 209 countries. The United States alone has more than 16,500 courses, over 40% of the world total, followed by Japan with around 3,200.
questions.source_title: R&A's Golf Around the World Report (National Golf Foundation)

questions.question: How many baby boys born in the US in 2023 were named Liam, the year's most popular name?
questions.explainer: Liam has topped the US boys' list every year since 2017, yet it accounts for barely 1% of boys born, a sign of how much more varied naming has become since the 1950s.
questions.source_title: Social Security Administration – Popular Baby Names

questions.question: How many different 5-card hands can be dealt from a standard 52-card deck?
questions.explainer: That is 52 choose 5. Only 4 of those hands are royal flushes, so the odds of being dealt one are about 1 in 650,000.

questions.question: How long is the Panama Canal from its Atlantic entrance to its Pacific entrance?
questions.explainer: At 82 km the canal is only about two marathons long, yet a ship transit takes 8 to 10 hours because of the locks and the crossing of Gatun Lake.

questions.question: What is the temperature at the core of the Sun in degrees Celsius?
questions.explainer: The core reaches about 15 million °C, hot enough to fuse hydrogen into helium, while the visible surface is a comparatively cool 5,500 °C.

questions.question: What is Pluto's average distance from the Sun in kilometres?
questions.explainer: Pluto orbits at about 39.5 times the Earth-Sun distance; sunlight takes around 5.5 hours to reach it, and New Horizons needed 9.5 years to get there.

questions.question: What was the fastest wind gust ever measured by an anemometer at Earth's surface (Barrow Island, Australia, 1996)?
questions.explainer: Tropical Cyclone Olivia produced a 3-second gust of 408 km/h (113 m/s) on 10 April 1996, ratified by the WMO in 2010. That is faster than a Formula 1 car at full speed.
questions.source_title: Fastest wind speed (recorded by an anemometer) - Guinness World Records

questions.question: On an average day in 2023, how many babies were born in Ireland?
questions.explainer: Ireland recorded about 54,500 births in 2023, down from a peak of around 75,000 in 2009, so each day brings roughly 150 newborns.
questions.source_title: Central Statistics Office (Ireland) – Vital Statistics Annual Report 2023

questions.question: How many ships made up the Spanish Armada that sailed against England in 1588?
questions.explainer: The fleet of 130 ships carried about 8,000 sailors and 18,000 soldiers. Storms around Scotland and Ireland sank more of them than English guns did.

questions.question: How many motor vehicles (cars, trucks and buses) were produced worldwide in 2023?
questions.explainer: China built about 30 million of them, nearly a third of the total. Worldwide that is roughly 180 vehicles rolling off a production line every minute.

questions.question: How many days did Pony Express riders take to carry mail from St. Joseph, Missouri, to Sacramento, California, in 1860?
questions.explainer: Relay riders covered roughly 1,900 miles in about 10 days, swapping horses every 10 to 15 miles. The telegraph killed the service after just 18 months.

questions.question: How many people died of tuberculosis worldwide in 2023?
questions.explainer: That made TB the world's deadliest infectious disease again after COVID-19 briefly took the top spot. About 10.8 million people fell ill with it that year.

questions.question: How many words are valid in Collins Scrabble Words 2019, the list used in tournaments outside North America?
questions.explainer: Every inflected form counts separately, so RUN, RUNS, RAN and RUNNING are four entries. The next edition, CSW21, trimmed about 400 offensive words from the list.

questions.question: How many main superconducting dipole magnets steer the beams around CERN's Large Hadron Collider ring?
questions.explainer: The LHC uses 1,232 dipole magnets, each 15 metres long and weighing about 35 tonnes, chilled to 1.9 K so they can bend protons around the 27 km ring with an 8.3 tesla field.
questions.source_title: Facts and figures about the LHC - CERN

questions.question: How many days did it take Meta's Threads app to reach 100 million sign-ups after it launched in July 2023?
questions.explainer: Threads launched on 5 July 2023 and Mark Zuckerberg announced 100 million sign-ups on 10 July, the fastest start of any consumer app, helped by one-tap sign-up with an existing Instagram account.

questions.question: How much did Microsoft pay to acquire Activision Blizzard in the deal that closed in October 2023?
questions.explainer: The largest video-game acquisition ever, about nine times Microsoft's 2021 purchase of Bethesda owner ZeniMax for $7.5 billion.
questions.source_title: Microsoft to acquire Activision Blizzard (Microsoft News)

questions.question: What is the density of osmium, the densest naturally occurring element, in kilograms per cubic metre?
questions.explainer: Osmium packs 22,590 kg into a cubic metre, more than 22 times the density of water and about twice that of lead; a one-litre bottle of it would weigh 22.6 kg, as much as a six-year-old child.

questions.question: How many US dollars did the United States transfer to Western Europe under the Marshall Plan between 1948 and 1952?
questions.explainer: The $13.3 billion sent over four years equals roughly $130 billion today and was around 5% of US GDP in 1948. The UK and France were the biggest recipients.

questions.question: How much did consumers spend on video games worldwide in 2024, according to Newzoo?
questions.explainer: Newzoo put 2024 consumer spending at about US$183 billion, roughly three times the global box office and recorded music industries combined; mobile games make up more than half of it.
questions.source_title: Newzoo Global Games Market Report 2025 (revised 2024 figure), via Game World Observer

questions.question: How long is Hadrian's Wall, from Wallsend on the River Tyne to Bowness-on-Solway?
questions.explainer: The wall ran 80 Roman miles, about 73 modern miles (117.5 km), coast to coast across northern England and was built in about six years starting in AD 122. That is roughly the distance from London to Birmingham.

questions.question: How many tonnes of honey were produced worldwide in 2022, according to FAO?
questions.explainer: Roughly 1.8 million tonnes a year, about 230 grams per person on Earth, with China by far the biggest producer.

questions.question: How many visitors did the Louvre museum in Paris receive in 2024?
questions.explainer: The Louvre is the world's most visited museum. 8.7 million visitors a year is about 24,000 a day, most of them from abroad.

questions.question: How many yen did the top bluefin tuna fetch at Tokyo's first fish auction of 2019, a record price?
questions.explainer: Sushi chain owner Kiyoshi Kimura paid 333.6 million yen (about US$3.1 million) for a 278 kg fish, over US$11,000 per kilogram.

questions.question: How many passengers were aboard the Mayflower when it sailed to America in 1620?
questions.explainer: 102 passengers plus around 30 crew spent 66 days crammed into a ship about 30 metres long. Roughly half the colonists died during the first winter.

questions.question: How much did the average new vehicle sold in the US weigh in model year 2022?
questions.explainer: A record 4,329 lb. The shift from sedans to SUVs and pickups has pushed the average up steadily since the early 1990s.
questions.source_title: U.S. EPA: The 2023 Automotive Trends Report - Highlights

questions.question: How many centimetres does human scalp hair grow in one year, on average?
questions.explainer: Scalp hair grows about 1.25 cm a month, so a hair that was never cut would take six to seven years to reach your waist.

questions.question: How much did Taylor Swift's Eras Tour (2023-2024) gross in ticket sales across its 149 shows?
questions.explainer: The Eras Tour was the first tour ever to gross more than US$1 billion and finished at about US$2.08 billion from roughly 10.2 million tickets, an average of about US$200 a ticket.

questions.question: How many views did the 'Baby Shark Dance' video have on YouTube by the end of 2024?
questions.explainer: Baby Shark Dance has been YouTube's most-viewed video since 2020 and was the first to pass 10 billion views in January 2022. 15 billion views is nearly two for every person on Earth.
questions.source_title: List of most-viewed YouTube videos - Wikipedia

questions.question: How many days did World War I last, from Austria-Hungary's declaration of war on 28 July 1914 to the armistice on 11 November 1918?
questions.explainer: The war ran for 4 years, 3 months and 2 weeks, about 1,568 days counting both the first and last day. Averaged over that span, roughly 6,000 soldiers died every single day.

questions.question: How many living languages are there in the world, as counted by Ethnologue in 2024?
questions.explainer: About 40% of those languages are endangered, while just 23 languages are spoken by more than half of the world's population.
questions.source_title: Ethnologue – How many languages are there in the world?

questions.question: How many kanji characters are on Japan's official joyo list for general use?
questions.explainer: The joyo kanji list, last revised in 2010, holds 2,136 characters that Japanese pupils learn by the end of secondary school; newspapers mostly keep to it.

questions.question: How many kilometres does Earth travel in one full orbit around the Sun?
questions.explainer: With an orbital radius of about 150 million km, Earth covers roughly 940 million km a year, moving at around 107,000 km/h.
questions.source_title: How big is Earth's orbit around the Sun? (Astronomy magazine)

questions.question: How many millimetres farther from Earth does the Moon drift each year?
questions.explainer: Lasers bounced off reflectors left by Apollo astronauts show the Moon receding about 3.8 cm a year, roughly the rate your fingernails grow.
questions.source_title: Measuring the Moon's Distance (NASA Eclipse Web Site)

questions.question: How many hectares of vineyards were planted worldwide in 2023, according to the OIV?
questions.explainer: That is about the land area of Ireland; Spain, France and China each have roughly 750,000-950,000 hectares under vine.
questions.source_title: OIV - State of the World Vine and Wine Sector in 2023

questions.question: What was the total prize pool of The International 2021, the Dota 2 world championship, in US$?
questions.explainer: Still the biggest prize pool for a single esports tournament, crowdfunded by Dota 2 players buying the in-game Battle Pass. Winners Team Spirit took home about US$18 million.
questions.source_title: Largest eSports prize pool for a single tournament (Guinness World Records)

questions.question: What was Apple's total revenue in its fiscal year 2024, which ended on 28 September 2024?
questions.explainer: iPhone alone brought in about $201 billion; Apple's annual revenue exceeds the GDP of countries such as Finland or Portugal.
questions.source_title: Apple reports fourth quarter results, FY2024 (Apple Newsroom)

questions.question: How fast does the International Space Station travel in its orbit, in km/h?
questions.explainer: At about 17,500 mph (28,000 km/h, or 7.7 km every second) the station circles Earth every 90 minutes, so the crew sees 16 sunrises a day.

questions.question: How much rain falls in an average year at Mawsynram, India, the wettest inhabited place on Earth?
questions.explainer: Nearly 12 metres of rain a year is about 20 times what London gets. Most of it falls in the monsoon months of June to September.

questions.question: How many islands make up the Philippines, according to the official NAMRIA count?
questions.explainer: Satellite mapping lifted the long-standing figure of 7,107 to 7,641. Only about 2,000 of the islands are inhabited and more than 5,000 still have no official name.
questions.source_title: List of islands of the Philippines - Wikipedia

questions.question: How many servings of Coca-Cola Company beverages are consumed worldwide every day, according to the company (as of 2024)?
questions.explainer: That is more than one serving a day for every four people on Earth, spread across the company's 200-plus brands from Coke to Fanta, Sprite and bottled water.

questions.question: What was the total GDP of the whole world in 2023, in current US dollars (World Bank)?
questions.explainer: The US made up roughly a quarter of it and China about a sixth. The whole world economy was only about $34 trillion in 2000.
questions.source_title: FRED / World Bank - Gross Domestic Product for World (NYGDPMKTPCDWLD)

questions.question: How fast is a point on the equator moving because of Earth's rotation alone (ignoring its orbit)?
questions.explainer: Earth's 40,075 km equatorial circumference divided by one sidereal day (23.93 h) gives about 1,674 km/h, faster than the speed of sound at sea level.

questions.question: How many copies of Wii Sports, the game bundled with the Nintendo Wii, were sold worldwide over its lifetime?
questions.explainer: Most copies came bundled with the console everywhere except Japan and South Korea, making it one of the best-selling games ever on a single platform.
questions.source_title: List of best-selling Wii video games - Wikipedia

questions.question: What was the median age at first marriage for men in the United States in 2023?
questions.explainer: American men now marry about seven years later than in 1960, when the median was 22.8; women's median in 2023 was 28.4.
questions.source_title: U.S. Census Bureau – Historical Marital Status Tables (Table MS-2)

questions.question: How long is the Gotthard Base Tunnel in Switzerland, the world's longest railway tunnel, in km?
questions.explainer: At 57 km the Gotthard Base Tunnel runs almost flat beneath the Alps, letting trains cross the mountains at full speed and cutting about an hour from Zurich-Milan journeys.

questions.question: What was India's GDP in 2023, in current US dollars (World Bank)?
questions.explainer: The fifth-largest economy in the world, behind the US, China, Germany and Japan. Spread over 1.4 billion people, that is only about $2,500 per person.
questions.source_title: FRED / World Bank - Gross Domestic Product for India (MKTGDPINA646NWDB)

questions.question: How many chickens were slaughtered for meat worldwide in 2022?
questions.explainer: Around 75 billion, more than nine chickens per person on Earth every year, or about 200 million every single day.
questions.source_title: Number of animals slaughtered for meat - Our World in Data

questions.question: How many gigawatt-hours of electricity did CERN consume in 2022?
questions.explainer: CERN used about 1,215 GWh in 2022, roughly what a mid-sized European city uses in a year, with demand peaking near 200 MW while the accelerators run.

questions.question: What is the total volume of planet Earth?
questions.explainer: Using 4/3 x pi x r³ with Earth's mean radius of 6,371 km gets you to about 1.08 trillion km³. The oceans account for only around 0.1% of that.

questions.question: What was McDonald's Corporation's total revenue in 2024, in US dollars?
questions.explainer: Most of that is rent and royalties from franchisees rather than burger sales; systemwide sales across all McDonald's restaurants were about US$130 billion.

questions.question: How many base pairs of DNA are in a single copy (haploid set) of the human genome?
questions.explainer: Stretched out, the DNA in one cell would be about 2 metres long, yet only around 1-2% of it codes for the roughly 20,000 proteins.

questions.question: How tall is Hyperion, the coast redwood in California that is the world's tallest known living tree, in metres?
questions.explainer: At about 116 m Hyperion is taller than the Statue of Liberty including its pedestal (93 m); its exact location is kept secret to protect it.

questions.question: How fast was the fastest badminton smash ever recorded (Guinness World Record, 2023), in km/h?
questions.explainer: Satwiksairaj Rankireddy's 565 km/h shot, measured in a controlled test, is faster than a Formula 1 car at full speed and more than twice the fastest tennis serve, though a shuttlecock slows down almost instantly.
questions.source_title: Indian shuttler Satwiksairaj Rankireddy sets Guinness world record for fastest badminton shot (All India Radio News)

questions.question: How many kilometres above the equator is a geostationary orbit?
questions.explainer: At 35,786 km a satellite's orbital period matches Earth's rotation, so it hangs over the same spot; that is nearly a tenth of the way to the Moon.

questions.question: How many entrants played the 2024 World Series of Poker Main Event in Las Vegas?
questions.explainer: A record field. At a US$10,000 buy-in it created a US$94 million prize pool, with US$10 million going to the winner.
questions.source_title: World Series of Poker Main Event sets another all-time record with 10,112 entries (Asia Gaming Brief)

questions.question: How many years did the Ottoman Empire last, from its founding around 1299 to its abolition in 1922?
questions.explainer: Founded by Osman I around 1299 and ended when the sultanate was abolished in November 1922, the empire spanned 623 years and 36 sultans. The United States has existed for less than half that time.

questions.question: How much does an average ostrich egg weigh, in grams?
questions.explainer: At 1.4 kg a single ostrich egg holds about as much as two dozen chicken eggs and takes around an hour and a half to hard-boil.

questions.question: How long is Australia's Great Barrier Reef, end to end along the Queensland coast?
questions.explainer: Made up of around 3,000 individual reefs and 900 islands, the Great Barrier Reef is roughly the length of the entire west coast of the contiguous United States.

questions.question: How many doses of COVID-19 vaccine had been administered worldwide by August 2024?
questions.explainer: That is about 1.7 doses for every person on Earth; roughly 70% of the world's population received at least one dose.

questions.question: How many nurses were working worldwide in 2023, according to the WHO?
questions.explainer: Nurses are the largest single group of health workers, yet the WHO still estimated a global shortfall of 5.8 million nurses in 2023, projected to shrink to about 4.1 million by 2030.
questions.source_title: Nursing and midwifery fact sheet (World Health Organization)

questions.question: How many runners finished the 2024 New York City Marathon?
questions.explainer: At the time a world record for any marathon, beating Berlin's 54,280 set just five weeks earlier. The very first NYC Marathon in 1970 had just 55 finishers.

questions.question: How many humans have ever been born in all of history, up to 2022?
questions.explainer: About 7% of everyone who has ever lived is alive today, so the claim that the living outnumber the dead is a myth.
questions.source_title: Population Reference Bureau – How Many People Have Ever Lived on Earth?

questions.question: How many people worldwide used the internet in 2024, according to the ITU's Facts and Figures 2024 report?
questions.explainer: About 68% of humanity; roughly 2.6 billion people were still offline, mostly in rural areas and low-income countries.
questions.source_title: ITU - Measuring digital development: Facts and Figures 2024

questions.question: How many months does an African elephant's pregnancy last?
questions.explainer: At about 22 months it is the longest gestation of any land mammal, nearly two and a half times a human pregnancy.

questions.question: What was Australia's population on 30 June 2024?
questions.explainer: Australia's population grew by about half a million in a single year, the bulk of it from overseas migration, on a landmass the size of the contiguous US.
questions.source_title: Australian Bureau of Statistics – National, state and territory population, June 2024

questions.question: What was Real Madrid's total revenue in the 2023/24 season, in euros (Deloitte Football Money League)?
questions.explainer: The first football club ever to pass €1 billion in a season: €248m matchday, €316m broadcast and €482m commercial. Manchester City was second at €838m.

questions.question: What was the total outstanding student loan debt in the United States at the end of 2023?
questions.explainer: Student loans are the second-largest category of US household debt after mortgages, spread across roughly 43 million borrowers, about US$37,000 each.
questions.source_title: Federal Reserve Bank of New York – Quarterly Report on Household Debt and Credit, Q4 2023

questions.question: How many eggs can a single female ocean sunfish carry at one time?
questions.explainer: Up to 300 million eggs, more than any other known vertebrate, each only about a millimetre across.

questions.question: In chess, how many different move sequences are possible in the first three moves by each player (six half-moves)?
questions.explainer: White has 20 possible first moves, there are 400 positions after Black replies, and the tree explodes from there: after four moves each it is about 85 billion.

questions.question: How many post boxes does Royal Mail have across the UK?
questions.explainer: Royal Mail aims to keep a post box within half a mile of 98% of addresses. Some boxes still in use date from the 1850s and carry Queen Victoria's cypher.

questions.question: How many tonnes of ultra-pure water fill the Super-Kamiokande neutrino detector in Japan?
questions.explainer: Super-K's stainless-steel tank, 39 m across and 41 m tall, holds 50,000 tonnes of ultra-pure water watched by about 11,000 photomultiplier tubes, a kilometre underground in a mine.

questions.question: How many neutrinos from the Sun pass through each square centimetre of Earth every second?
questions.explainer: About 65 billion solar neutrinos cross every square centimetre of your body each second, day and night, yet on average only one will interact with you in your whole lifetime.

questions.question: How many daily active users did Reddit report for the fourth quarter of 2024?
questions.explainer: Reddit calls them 'daily active uniques'; just over half are outside the United States, and the figure grew 39% in a single year.
questions.source_title: Reddit Q4 and Full Year 2024 Results (Reddit Investor Relations)

questions.question: How old was Methuselah, the Great Basin bristlecone pine in California's White Mountains, in 2024?
questions.explainer: It germinated around 2833 BC, before the Great Pyramid of Giza was built, and is still alive today.

questions.question: How tall, in centimetres, was Robert Wadlow, the tallest person in recorded history, at his last measurement in 1940?
questions.explainer: That is 8 feet 11 inches. Wadlow was still growing when he died at 22 from an infected blister caused by a leg brace.

questions.question: What is the voltage, in volts, of the world's highest-voltage power transmission line (China's Changji-Guquan link)?
questions.explainer: The 1,100 kV DC line carries 12,000 MW over 3,300 km from Xinjiang to eastern China, nearly 5,000 times the 230 V of a European household socket.

questions.question: What is the maximum takeoff weight of an Airbus A380, the world's largest passenger airliner, in tonnes?
questions.explainer: The heaviest-certified A380 variant can weigh 575 tonnes at takeoff (the original version was rated at 560 t), roughly the weight of 100 adult African elephants, with fuel making up a large share of that.

questions.question: At what frequency, in megahertz, does a standard domestic microwave oven heat food?
questions.explainer: Home microwave ovens run at 2,450 MHz, giving a wavelength of about 12 cm, in the same 2.4 GHz band shared by Wi-Fi and Bluetooth.

questions.question: How many billionaires were on Forbes' 2024 list of the world's billionaires?
questions.explainer: A record, with 813 of them in the US. Their combined wealth of $14.2 trillion exceeded the GDP of every country except the US and China.
questions.source_title: Forbes - The World's Billionaires 2024 (as reported by AP)

questions.question: How many kilocalories of energy are stored in one kilogram of human body fat?
questions.explainer: This is the famous '3,500 calories per pound' rule: a 500 kcal daily deficit would, in principle, burn off a kilogram of fat in about two weeks.
questions.source_title: What is the required energy deficit per unit weight loss? (Hall, International Journal of Obesity, 2008)

questions.question: How many different positions can a standard 3x3 Rubik's Cube be scrambled into?
questions.explainer: About 43 quintillion. Visiting one position per second would take 1.4 trillion years, 100 times the age of the universe, yet any position can be solved in 20 moves or fewer.

questions.question: What is the trunk volume of General Sherman, the giant sequoia in California that is the largest tree on Earth, in cubic metres?
questions.explainer: About 1,487 cubic metres of wood in one trunk, enough to fill more than half an Olympic swimming pool.

questions.question: What was the world's GDP per person in 2023, in current US dollars (World Bank)?
questions.explainer: Roughly $107 trillion of output shared among 8 billion people. The US figure is about six times this; India's is about a fifth of it.
questions.source_title: FRED / World Bank - Gross Domestic Product Per Capita for World (NYGDPPCAPCDWLD)

questions.question: How much money, in Swedish kronor, came with each full Nobel Prize awarded in 2023?
questions.explainer: Up from 10 million kronor the year before, worth about US$1 million at 2023 exchange rates. A prize shared by three laureates is split between them.

questions.question: How many children and youth worldwide were out of school in 2023, according to UNESCO?
questions.explainer: That is roughly one in six school-age children and youth, and 6 million more than in 2021, partly because of the exclusion of girls and women from education in Afghanistan.
questions.source_title: UNESCO – 250 million children out-of-school: What you need to know about UNESCO's latest education data

questions.question: How tall is the Mona Lisa painting itself, excluding its frame?
questions.explainer: The Mona Lisa measures just 77 by 53 cm, a little smaller than an A1 poster. Many Louvre visitors are surprised by how small it is.

questions.question: How many countries does the Danube River flow through or along on its course from Germany to the Black Sea?
questions.explainer: The Danube passes through or borders Germany, Austria, Slovakia, Hungary, Croatia, Serbia, Bulgaria, Romania, Moldova and Ukraine: more countries than any other river on Earth.

questions.question: How many people died of malaria worldwide in 2023?
questions.explainer: There were about 263 million malaria cases that year. Roughly three-quarters of the deaths were children under five in sub-Saharan Africa.

questions.question: How many bacterial cells live in or on the body of a typical 70 kg adult?
questions.explainer: That is close to the 30 trillion human cells in the same body, so the old '10 bacteria for every human cell' claim is really about one to one. Most of them live in the colon.
questions.source_title: Revised Estimates for the Number of Human and Bacteria Cells in the Body (Sender, Fuchs & Milo, PLOS Biology 2016)

questions.question: How many paid subscribers did Netflix have worldwide at the end of 2024?
questions.explainer: Netflix added a record 19 million subscribers in the final quarter of 2024 alone, then stopped reporting quarterly subscriber counts from 2025.
questions.source_title: Netflix Q4 2024 Shareholder Letter (Netflix Investor Relations)

questions.question: How many days did the Berlin Wall stand, from 13 August 1961 to 9 November 1989?
questions.explainer: The wall divided Berlin for 28 years, 2 months and 27 days, about 10,316 days counting both the first and last day. On 5 February 2018 it had been gone for exactly as long as it had stood.

questions.question: How much did Americans spend on their pets in 2024, in US$, per the American Pet Products Association?
questions.explainer: About $152 billion, or roughly $450 for every person in the United States, with food and treats the biggest slice of the bill.
questions.source_title: Industry Trends and Stats - American Pet Products Association

questions.question: How many children worldwide died before their fifth birthday in 2023?
questions.explainer: That is about 13,000 young children a day, but it is down from 12.8 million a year in 1990, one of the biggest public-health wins in history.
questions.source_title: Levels and Trends in Child Mortality: Report 2024 (UN IGME / UNICEF)

questions.question: How much does a Paris 2024 Olympic gold medal weigh, in grams?
questions.explainer: About the weight of a can of soup: 505 g of silver, 18 g of Eiffel Tower iron and a thin gold plating. The silver medal weighs 525 g and the bronze 455 g.
questions.source_title: Olympic and Paralympic medals for Paris 2024 revealed (ITF)

questions.question: How many miles did all motor vehicles drive on US roads in 2023?
questions.explainer: Americans drove about 3.26 trillion miles in 2023, close to 9,700 miles per person, or roughly 17,500 return trips between the Earth and the Sun.

questions.question: What was the average age of cars and light trucks on US roads in 2024?
questions.explainer: US vehicles keep getting older: the average was about 9.6 years in 2002. Better build quality and high new-car prices keep old cars on the road longer.
questions.source_title: Bureau of Transportation Statistics: Average Age of Automobiles and Trucks in Operation in the United States

questions.question: What top speed in km/h did Usain Bolt reach during his 9.58-second 100 m world record in 2009?
questions.explainer: That is 12.4 metres per second, reached between the 60 m and 80 m marks. Over the whole race he averaged 37.6 km/h.

questions.question: How many litres of water does an Olympic-size swimming pool (50 m long, 25 m wide, 2 m deep) hold?
questions.explainer: That is 2,500 cubic metres, or about 2,500 tonnes of water - enough to fill roughly 16,000 bathtubs or supply a US family's home for about six years.

questions.question: How many pixels does the LSST camera at the Vera C. Rubin Observatory capture in a single image?
questions.explainer: The 3,200-megapixel LSST camera is the largest digital camera ever built; displaying one of its images at full resolution would take about 400 ultra-HD TV screens.
questions.source_title: Largest camera ever built arrives at Rubin Observatory in Chile - NSF

questions.question: How many McDonald's restaurants were operating worldwide at the end of 2024?
questions.explainer: Roughly 95% of them are run by franchisees across more than 100 countries; the United States alone has around 13,500 McDonald's.

questions.question: What was the launch mass of the James Webb Space Telescope in kilograms?
questions.explainer: Webb weighed about 6,200 kg at launch (6,161 kg by the detailed figure), roughly a bull African elephant, and about half of Hubble's 11,100 kg despite a mirror with six times the area.

questions.question: What was the peak weight in kilograms of Jon Brower Minnoch, the heaviest person ever recorded, in 1978?
questions.explainer: That is about 1,400 pounds, roughly the weight of a small car. Much of it was fluid retained because of heart failure.

questions.question: What is the top speed in regular service of Japan's fastest Shinkansen trains, on the Tohoku line, in km/h?
questions.explainer: The E5 and H5 trains run at 320 km/h in service, about 89 metres every second, enough to cover a football pitch in just over a second.

questions.question: What was the total worldwide cinema box office in 2023, in US dollars?
questions.explainer: Up 31% on 2022 thanks to Barbie, Oppenheimer and Super Mario, but still 15% below the pre-pandemic average. North America made up about $9 billion.
questions.source_title: Gower Street Analytics - 2023 global box office estimated at $33.9 billion

questions.question: How many grams of sugar are in a 330 ml can of Coca-Cola Original Taste sold in the UK?
questions.explainer: That is almost nine teaspoons of sugar in one can, more than the 30 g of free sugars per day the UK NHS recommends as an adult's maximum.
questions.source_title: Coca-Cola Great Britain - Coca-Cola Original Taste nutrition

questions.question: What is the half-life of uranium-238, in years?
questions.explainer: U-238's half-life of 4.47 billion years is almost exactly the age of the Earth, so about half of the uranium-238 present when the planet formed is still here.

questions.question: What is the installed generating capacity of China's Three Gorges Dam, in megawatts?
questions.explainer: Its 34 generators add up to 22,500 MW, the largest power station on Earth, equivalent to roughly 20 big nuclear reactors.

questions.question: How many Earth years does Neptune take to complete one orbit of the Sun?
questions.explainer: Neptune was discovered in 1846 and only completed its first observed orbit in 2011; a Neptunian year is 164.8 Earth years.

questions.question: How many performances did The Phantom of the Opera give on Broadway before it closed in April 2023?
questions.explainer: Phantom opened in January 1988 and ran for 35 years at about eight shows a week, making it by far the longest-running show in Broadway history.
questions.source_title: The Phantom of the Opera (1986 musical) - Wikipedia

questions.question: How many hectares of forest did the world have in 2020, per the FAO Global Forest Resources Assessment?
questions.explainer: 4.06 billion hectares, about 31% of all land, or roughly half a hectare of forest for every person alive.

questions.question: How many Allied soldiers were evacuated from Dunkirk between 26 May and 4 June 1940?
questions.explainer: Operation Dynamo brought 338,226 British and French soldiers home in nine days using over 800 vessels, from destroyers to fishing boats. Churchill had hoped to save perhaps 30,000.

questions.question: How long is the Trans-Siberian Railway from Moscow to Vladivostok, in km?
questions.explainer: The Moscow-Vladivostok line is 9,289 km long and crosses eight time zones; the through train takes about a week from end to end.

questions.question: How much did the US federal government spend in total in fiscal year 2023 (October 2022 to September 2023)?
questions.explainer: Around $18,000 per US resident. Receipts were $4.4 trillion, leaving a $1.7 trillion deficit; Social Security and interest on the debt alone topped $2 trillion.
questions.source_title: US Treasury - Combined Statement of Receipts, Outlays, and Balances FY2023: Outlays

questions.question: How much did SoFi Stadium in Los Angeles, opened in 2020, cost to build, in US$?
questions.explainer: The most expensive stadium ever built, privately financed by Rams owner Stan Kroenke. It cost more than twice as much as any other NFL stadium.
questions.source_title: New report ranks the 30 most expensive sports venues (Construction Dive)

questions.question: How many spider species had been scientifically described worldwide, per the World Spider Catalog, as of 2024?
questions.explainer: Over 52,000 named species, with hundreds more added every year; taxonomists suspect the true number may be double that.

questions.question: How tall is Angel Falls in Venezuela, the world's tallest waterfall, from top to bottom?
questions.explainer: At 979 m, Angel Falls is nearly three times the height of the Eiffel Tower, with an uninterrupted plunge of 807 m before the water hits the rocks below.

questions.question: What is the area of the Sahara Desert?
questions.explainer: The Sahara covers about 30% of Africa and is nearly the size of the United States or China. Only Antarctica and the Arctic are larger deserts.

questions.question: How many rides were taken on the New York City Subway in 2023?
questions.explainer: About 3.2 million rides on an average day across 472 stations - still only around two-thirds of the 1.7 billion rides of 2019.
questions.source_title: MTA: Subway and bus ridership for 2023

questions.question: How many smartphones were shipped worldwide in 2024, according to IDC?
questions.explainer: That is about one new phone for every 6.5 people on Earth; Apple shipped about 232 million of them and Samsung about 223 million.

questions.question: How fast does Earth travel along its orbit around the Sun, in kilometres per hour?
questions.explainer: Earth orbits the Sun at about 29.8 km/s, or 107,000 km/h, covering its own diameter every seven minutes and a full 940-million-kilometre loop each year.

questions.question: What is the total length of all sections of the Great Wall of China, as measured in China's 2012 national survey?
questions.explainer: Counting every dynasty's walls, trenches and natural barriers, the 2012 survey came to 21,196 km, more than half the circumference of the Earth. The Ming-era wall alone is about 8,850 km.

questions.question: How many km of public roads does the United States have, as of 2022?
questions.explainer: The US has about 6.7 million km (4.2 million miles) of public roads, enough to drive to the Moon and back more than eight times.

questions.question: On an average day in 2023, how many people died in Japan?
questions.explainer: Japan recorded about 1.58 million deaths in 2023 against only 727,000 births, so the population shrinks by more than 2,000 people every day.

questions.question: How many different completed 9x9 Sudoku grids exist?
questions.explainer: About 6.7 sextillion, computed by Felgenhauer and Jarvis in 2005. Strip out rotations, reflections and relabelings and 'only' 5.47 billion essentially different grids remain.

questions.question: How many tonnes of green coffee beans were produced worldwide in the 2023/24 coffee year, per the ICO?
questions.explainer: That is about 178 million standard 60 kg bags; Brazil grows roughly a third of the world's coffee and Vietnam about a sixth.
questions.source_title: International Coffee Organization - Coffee Report and Outlook, December 2023

questions.question: What share of the world's population lived in urban areas in 2023?
questions.explainer: Humanity crossed the 50% urban mark around 2007; the UN expects more than two-thirds of people to live in cities by 2050.
questions.source_title: World Bank – Urban population (% of total population)

questions.question: How many neurons are in an adult human brain?
questions.explainer: The older '100 billion' figure was a rough guess; a 2009 cell count found 86 billion neurons, plus a similar number of non-neuronal glial cells.
questions.source_title: List of animals by number of neurons (Wikipedia)

questions.question: How much did World War II cost the United States military, in constant FY2011 US dollars, per the Congressional Research Service?
questions.explainer: CRS puts the bill at about $296 billion in 1940s dollars, or $4.1 trillion in FY2011 dollars. At its peak in 1945, war spending was nearly 36% of US GDP.
questions.source_title: Costs of Major U.S. Wars (CRS report RS22926)

questions.question: What was the population of Indonesia in mid-2023?
questions.explainer: Indonesia is the world's fourth most populous country, and more than half its people live on the single island of Java.
questions.source_title: Wikipedia – Demographics of Indonesia (Statistics Indonesia / BPS estimates)

questions.question: At what price per share did Apple sell its stock in its initial public offering on 12 December 1980?
questions.explainer: The 4.6 million shares raised about $100 million and valued Apple near $1.8 billion by the close of its first day. Thanks to five splits, one of those $22 shares is now 224 shares.
questions.source_title: TechCrunch - A look back in IPO: Apple, the early PC purveyor

questions.question: How many living bird species were recognised on the IOC World Bird List as of 2024?
questions.explainer: Around 11,000 species, roughly 6,500 of them passerines (perching birds), and a handful of new species are still described every year.

questions.question: How many passengers passed through London Heathrow Airport in 2024?
questions.explainer: Heathrow's record 83.9 million passengers in 2024 is about 230,000 a day, all handled on just two runways.

questions.question: How much revenue did the global recorded music industry earn in 2024, according to IFPI?
questions.explainer: Recorded music earned US$29.6 billion in 2024, its tenth straight year of growth, with streaming providing about two-thirds of the total.

questions.question: How many gold marks did the 1921 London Schedule of Payments set as Germany's total World War I reparations bill?
questions.explainer: The headline figure of 132 billion gold marks was about US$33 billion at the time, though only 50 billion was ever seriously expected to be paid. Germany made its final payment in 2010.

questions.question: How many tonnes of food did households, food service and retail waste worldwide in 2022, per the UNEP Food Waste Index?
questions.explainer: That is about 132 kg per person per year, roughly a fifth of all food available to consumers; households alone account for about 60% of it.

questions.question: How many guests visited Magic Kingdom at Walt Disney World in Florida in 2023?
questions.explainer: Magic Kingdom has been the world's most visited theme park for decades. 17.7 million guests a year works out to nearly 50,000 every day.

questions.question: How many earthquakes of magnitude 7.0 or greater were recorded worldwide in 2023?
questions.explainer: USGS counts about 15 magnitude-7 quakes in a typical year, so 2023's 19 was a little above average. The February Turkey-Syria doublet (M7.8 and M7.5) made it a deadly year, with roughly 60,000 deaths.
questions.source_title: Earthquake Lists, Maps, and Statistics - USGS

questions.question: What was the population of the Republic of Ireland in April 2024?
questions.explainer: Ireland's population passed 5 million in 2021 for the first time since the 1851 census, taken just after the Great Famine, driven mostly by immigration.
questions.source_title: Central Statistics Office (Ireland) – Population and Migration Estimates, April 2024

questions.question: What is the total volume of water in all of Earth's oceans?
questions.explainer: About 1.335 billion cubic kilometres, or 97% of all water on Earth. Spread evenly over the whole globe it would form a layer around 2.6 km deep.
questions.source_title: How much water is in the ocean? - NOAA National Ocean Service

questions.question: What was the gross national debt of the United States on 31 December 2024?
questions.explainer: About $106,000 per US resident and growing by roughly $2 trillion a year. The debt first crossed $36 trillion in November 2024, only four months after passing $35 trillion.
questions.source_title: US Treasury - Monthly Statement of the Public Debt, December 2024

questions.question: How many metres long was the longest pizza ever made, baked in Fontana, California in 2017 (Guinness World Record)?
questions.explainer: The pizza stretched almost 2 km, about 18 football pitches end to end, and was baked by ovens rolling along a conveyor before being donated to food banks.

questions.question: How long is the Bayeux Tapestry, the embroidered cloth depicting the Norman conquest of 1066?
questions.explainer: The tapestry is almost 70 metres long but only 50 cm tall, about the length of three tennis courts laid end to end.

questions.question: How many tornadoes were confirmed in the United States in 2023?
questions.explainer: The US averages roughly 1,200 tornadoes a year, more than any other country. A single outbreak on 31 March to 1 April 2023 produced well over 100 of them across the Midwest and South.

questions.question: How many minutes did the average US worker spend travelling to work, one way, in 2023?
questions.explainer: Round trip, that is nearly an hour a day - roughly 220 hours a year, or more than five full working weeks spent getting to and from work.
questions.source_title: U.S. Census Bureau, American Community Survey 2023 1-Year Estimates, Table S0801 Commuting Characteristics

questions.question: How many African elephants (savanna and forest) were estimated to remain in the wild in 2016, per the IUCN status report?
questions.explainer: About 415,000, down from several million a century ago; Botswana alone is home to roughly a third of them.

questions.question: How many pieces of mail did the US Postal Service handle in fiscal year 2023?
questions.explainer: That is about 318 million pieces every day, delivered to roughly 167 million addresses - and still close to half of all the mail sent in the world.
questions.source_title: USPS Postal Facts: Size and Scope

questions.question: How many kilograms of Moon rock and soil did the six Apollo landings bring back to Earth in total?
questions.explainer: About 382 kg in 2,196 individual samples, roughly the weight of a grand piano, most of it still stored at Johnson Space Center in Houston.
questions.source_title: Lunar Samples (NASA Astromaterials Acquisition and Curation Office)

questions.question: How many lines of verse are there in Homer's Iliad?
questions.explainer: The Iliad's 15,693 lines are divided into 24 books. Recited aloud at a storyteller's pace, the whole poem takes roughly 20 hours.

questions.question: How many kilocalories are in a McDonald's Big Mac in the US, according to McDonald's own nutrition facts?
questions.explainer: Add a medium fries (about 320 kcal) and a medium Coke (about 200 kcal) and the meal passes 1,100 kcal, roughly half of an adult's daily energy needs.

questions.question: How many containers (TEU) did the Port of Shanghai, the world's busiest container port, handle in 2024?
questions.explainer: Shanghai handled 51.5 million TEU in 2024, the first port ever to pass 50 million, which works out to nearly 6,000 containers every hour around the clock.

questions.question: How many transistors are on Apple's M2 Ultra chip, released in 2023?
questions.explainer: The M2 Ultra fuses two M2 Max dies into one; 134 billion transistors is about 58 million times the count of the 1971 Intel 4004.

questions.question: How many 3.5-inch floppy disks did the retail floppy edition of Windows 95 ship on in 1995?
questions.explainer: Microsoft used a special 1.68 MB 'DMF' disk format to squeeze Windows 95 onto 13 disks instead of the usual 1.44 MB ones; Windows NT 3.1 had needed 22 floppies two years earlier.

questions.question: How many near-Earth asteroids had been discovered as of the end of 2025?
questions.explainer: Around 40,000 near-Earth asteroids were catalogued by the end of 2025, with roughly 3,000 new ones found each year; fewer than 900 of them are larger than 1 km.
questions.source_title: Discovery Statistics: Cumulative Totals (NASA JPL Center for Near-Earth Object Studies)

questions.question: How much funding did the US Congress give NASA for fiscal year 2024?
questions.explainer: About 0.4% of federal spending, and NASA's first year-on-year cut since 2013. At its 1960s Apollo peak NASA took more than 4% of the federal budget.
questions.source_title: The Planetary Society - NASA's FY 2024 Budget

questions.question: How many grams of pure gold are in a Paris 2024 Olympic gold medal?
questions.explainer: The 'gold' medal is 95% silver with just 6 g of gold plating, worth roughly US$1,000 in raw metal at 2024 prices. It also contains 18 g of iron taken from the Eiffel Tower.
questions.source_title: Here's how much the Paris 2024 Olympic gold medal is actually worth (Forbes Australia)

questions.question: How many web pages had the Internet Archive's Wayback Machine archived by October 2025?
questions.explainer: The Internet Archive marked the one-trillion-page milestone in October 2025; the Wayback Machine has been saving snapshots since 1996 and now archives hundreds of millions of URLs a day.

questions.question: How many digits of pi were computed in the world-record calculation completed in April 2025?
questions.explainer: Linus Media Group and Kioxia ran the y-cruncher program for about seven and a half months to reach 300 trillion digits; NASA uses only about 15 digits for interplanetary navigation.
questions.source_title: Chronology of computation of pi - Wikipedia

questions.question: How long is the Nile River from its most distant headwater to the Mediterranean Sea?
questions.explainer: At 6,650 km the Nile is about 1,000 km longer than the flight from London to New York. Its exact length is debated, and rival measurements favour the Amazon as the longest river.

questions.question: How many times more massive is the Sun than Earth?
questions.explainer: The Sun holds 99.8% of the Solar System's mass; Earth would need to be duplicated about 333,000 times to match it.

questions.question: How many litres of water does it take on average worldwide to produce 1 kg of beef, counting feed, drinking and processing?
questions.explainer: Almost all of that water goes into growing cattle feed; by the same method 1 kg of chicken needs about 4,300 litres and 1 kg of wheat about 1,800 litres.
questions.source_title: Water Footprint Network - Product water footprint gallery (Mekonnen & Hoekstra)

questions.question: How many litres of fluid do a healthy adult's kidneys filter from the blood each day?
questions.explainer: Nearly all of it is reabsorbed: only about 1.5 litres leaves the body as urine, so the kidneys reclaim over 99% of what they filter.

questions.question: How many years old is New York's Brooklyn Bridge in 2026, counting from its opening?
questions.explainer: The bridge opened on 24 May 1883 as the longest suspension bridge in the world, and more than 140 years later it still carries cars, cyclists and walkers across the East River.

questions.question: How many organ transplants were performed in the United States in 2023?
questions.explainer: Kidneys make up well over half of these. The annual total has set a new record every year since 2013, yet more than 100,000 Americans remain on the waiting list.
questions.source_title: Continued increase in organ donation drives new records in 2023 (OPTN / UNOS)

questions.question: How old is the Acasta Gneiss in Canada, one of the oldest known rock formations on Earth?
questions.explainer: At 4.03 billion years, this outcrop in Canada's Northwest Territories formed when Earth was barely 500 million years old. Only a few zircon crystals are older.

questions.question: How many litres of water does the average American family use at home per day, according to the EPA?
questions.explainer: That is more than 300 US gallons, and roughly 70% of it is used indoors - toilets, showers and taps are the big three.
questions.source_title: U.S. EPA WaterSense: How We Use Water

questions.question: How many official languages does the European Union have?
questions.explainer: With 27 member states but 24 languages, every EU law is translated into all of them, and the European Parliament runs one of the largest interpreting services in the world.

questions.question: What is the life expectancy at birth for women in Japan, according to the 2023 official life table?
questions.explainer: Japanese women have the longest life expectancy of any large population; Japanese men come in at about 81 years, a gap of roughly six years.
questions.source_title: Ministry of Health, Labour and Welfare (Japan) – Abridged Life Tables for Japan 2023

questions.question: How much water does the Amazon River discharge into the Atlantic every second, on average?
questions.explainer: The Amazon carries about 20% of all the river water that reaches the world's oceans, and more than the next seven largest rivers combined.

questions.question: How many bridges are there in the United States, according to the National Bridge Inventory?
questions.explainer: Almost half are more than 50 years old, and roughly 7% are rated in poor condition - yet they carry well over 100 million crossings a day.

questions.question: How many Nintendo Switch consoles had been sold worldwide as of 31 March 2025?
questions.explainer: That puts the Switch just behind the Nintendo DS (154 million) and the PlayStation 2 (about 160 million) among the best-selling consoles of all time.
questions.source_title: Nintendo IR - Dedicated Video Game Sales Units

questions.question: How many Starbucks stores were open worldwide at the end of fiscal year 2024 (September 2024)?
questions.explainer: Starbucks passed 40,000 stores for the first time in 2024; about 17,000 are in the US and nearly 8,000 in China, its second-largest market.
questions.source_title: Starbucks Q4 Fiscal Year 2024 Results press release

questions.question: How many enslaved Africans were embarked on ships in the transatlantic slave trade between the 16th and 19th centuries?
questions.explainer: The Trans-Atlantic Slave Trade Database documents about 12.5 million people embarked, of whom roughly 10.7 million survived the Middle Passage. Brazil alone received nearly 5 million.

questions.question: What was the official attendance at the deciding match of the 1950 World Cup, Brazil v Uruguay, at the Maracanã?
questions.explainer: Still the largest official crowd at any World Cup match; unofficial counts put it near 200,000. Uruguay's 2–1 win is remembered in Brazil as the 'Maracanazo'.
questions.source_title: Largest attendance at a FIFA World Cup match (Guinness World Records)

questions.question: How many people became naturalized US citizens in fiscal year 2023?
questions.explainer: FY2023 was one of the busiest years for naturalizations in US history; Mexico, India and the Philippines were the top countries of origin.

questions.question: How deep is Lake Baikal in Siberia at its deepest point?
questions.explainer: Baikal is the deepest lake on Earth and holds about one fifth of the world's unfrozen fresh surface water. Four Eiffel Towers stacked in it would still be 300 m short of the surface.

questions.question: How many tonnes of cargo were shipped by sea worldwide in 2023?
questions.explainer: Ships carried about 12.3 billion tonnes of goods in 2023, roughly 1.5 tonnes for every person on Earth; oil, iron ore, coal and grain make up most of it.

questions.question: How many international students were enrolled at US colleges and universities in the 2023/24 academic year?
questions.explainer: A record year: India overtook China as the top sending country, and international students made up about 6% of all US higher-education enrolment.

questions.question: How much did the world's governments spend on their militaries in 2023, according to SIPRI?
questions.explainer: A record, equal to 2.3% of world GDP or $306 per person on Earth. The US alone accounted for $916 billion, about 37% of the total.
questions.source_title: SIPRI - Trends in World Military Expenditure, 2023

questions.question: How many popes has the Catholic Church had in total, counting Pope Leo XIV elected in 2025?
questions.explainer: Leo XIV is counted as the 267th pope in a line that starts with Saint Peter. That works out to an average reign of a little over seven years.

questions.question: How many oil paintings did Vincent van Gogh produce in his lifetime?
questions.explainer: Van Gogh painted around 860 oil paintings, almost all in the last ten years of his life, close to two a week, and sold only a handful before he died in 1890.

questions.question: How much electricity did the world's data centres consume in 2024, according to the International Energy Agency?
questions.explainer: That is about 1.5% of global electricity use, roughly what France consumes in a year; the IEA expects it to more than double to about 945 TWh by 2030, driven largely by AI.
questions.source_title: IEA - Energy and AI, Executive summary

questions.question: How many days did Valeri Polyakov spend in space on his record single flight aboard the Mir station (1994-95)?
questions.explainer: The physician-cosmonaut stayed aloft 437 days and 18 hours, more than 14 months, a record that still stands; Frank Rubio's 371 days is the US record.

questions.question: How many litres of wine were produced worldwide in 2023, according to the OIV?
questions.explainer: At 237 million hectolitres it was then the smallest harvest since 1961, hit by drought and frost (2024 came in lower still), yet enough for about 32 billion 750 ml bottles.
questions.source_title: OIV - State of the World Vine and Wine Sector in 2023

questions.question: What was the median US household income in 2023, according to the Census Bureau?
questions.explainer: Up 4% in real terms from 2022, the first significant rise since 2019. Half of US households earned more than this and half earned less.
questions.source_title: US Census Bureau - Income in the United States: 2023 (P60-282)

questions.question: How many laps of the 27 km Large Hadron Collider ring does a proton complete every second?
questions.explainer: Travelling at 99.9999991% of the speed of light, each proton circles the 26.7 km ring 11,245 times a second, covering a distance equal to seven and a half trips around the Earth.
questions.source_title: Facts and figures about the LHC - CERN

questions.question: How many Jews were there in the world in 2023 (core Jewish population)?
questions.explainer: The world Jewish population still has not regained its 1939 level of about 16.6 million; Israel and the United States account for roughly 85% of the total.
questions.source_title: Wikipedia – Jewish population by country (Jewish Agency / DellaPergola estimates)

questions.question: How many kilocalories are in one level teaspoon (4 g) of white granulated sugar?
questions.explainer: A teaspoon of sugar weighs about 4 g and every gram of sugar carries 4 kcal, so each spoonful in your tea adds roughly 16 kcal.

questions.question: How many kilometres from Earth does the James Webb Space Telescope orbit, at the Sun-Earth L2 point?
questions.explainer: Webb sits about four times farther away than the Moon, far too distant for any repair mission, unlike Hubble in low Earth orbit.
questions.source_title: Webb's Orbit at Sun-Earth Lagrange Point 2 (NASA Science)

questions.question: How many adults worldwide were living with obesity in 2022?
questions.explainer: Counting children too, about one in eight people on the planet was living with obesity. Worldwide adult obesity has more than doubled since 1990.
questions.source_title: Obesity and overweight fact sheet (World Health Organization)

questions.question: What is NASA's estimated lifetime cost of the James Webb Space Telescope, in US dollars?
questions.explainer: NASA's share is about $9.7 billion over 24 years, including five years of operations, roughly double the early estimates; ESA and Canada added around another $1 billion.
questions.source_title: How much does the James Webb Space Telescope cost? (The Planetary Society)

questions.question: What was the land area of the Mongol Empire at its greatest extent, around 1309?
questions.explainer: At its peak the empire covered about 24 million square kilometres, roughly 16% of Earth's land, stretching from Korea to Hungary. Only the British Empire has ever been larger.

questions.question: How much did London's Crossrail, now the Elizabeth line, cost to build, in pounds sterling?
questions.explainer: The Elizabeth line opened in 2022 at a final cost of about £18.8 billion, around £160 million for every kilometre of its 118 km route.

questions.question: What price, including fees, did Leonardo da Vinci's Salvator Mundi fetch at Christie's in New York in November 2017?
questions.explainer: Still the most expensive artwork ever sold at auction, more than double the previous record. The same painting sold for £45 in 1958 when it was thought to be a copy.
questions.source_title: WAMC/NPR - Leonardo da Vinci portrait of Christ sells for record-shattering $450 million
