questions.question: What is the deepest dive ever recorded for a Cuvier's beaked whale, the deepest-diving mammal, in metres?
questions.explainer: Nearly 3 km straight down, close to seven Empire State Buildings stacked end to end; the same species has also been logged holding its breath for more than three hours.

questions.question: How many places (settlements) are recorded in the Domesday Book, England's great survey completed in 1086?
questions.explainer: William the Conqueror's surveyors recorded 13,418 places in under a year, nearly every town and village in England south of the Tees. Most of those settlements still exist today.

questions.question: How many cents did a US First-Class Forever stamp cost after the price rise of 14 July 2024?
questions.explainer: It was the second increase of 2024, up from 68 cents in January. A first-class stamp cost 20 cents in 1981.
questions.source_title: CBS News - Stamp prices poised to rise again, for the 2nd time this year

questions.question: What is the annual salary of the President of the United States, as set by law since 2001?
questions.explainer: Doubled from $200,000 in 2001, plus a $50,000 expense allowance. Inflation has since eroded the salary's buying power by roughly 40%.
questions.source_title: 3 U.S. Code § 102 - Compensation of the President (govinfo)

questions.question: How many monthly active users did Facebook have as of 31 December 2023?
questions.explainer: That is roughly 38% of all humans. Meta stopped reporting Facebook-only user numbers in 2024, so this is the last official figure.
questions.source_title: Meta Reports Fourth Quarter and Full Year 2023 Results (Meta Investor Relations)

questions.question: How many kilometres from Earth was Voyager 1 in mid-2025?
questions.explainer: Launched in 1977, Voyager 1 passed 25 billion km (about 167 times the Earth-Sun distance) in 2025, so far that radio signals take nearly a full day to reach it.
questions.source_title: Voyager 1 is about to be one light-day from Earth (BBC Sky at Night Magazine)

questions.question: What is the longest non-stop flight recorded for a bird (a bar-tailed godwit tracked from Alaska to Tasmania in 2022), in km?
questions.explainer: The five-month-old godwit flew 13,560 km in 11 days without stopping to eat, drink or rest, about a third of the way around the world.

questions.question: How many hot dogs do Americans eat on the Fourth of July, according to the National Hot Dog and Sausage Council?
questions.explainer: Laid end to end, 150 million hot dogs would stretch from Washington, DC to Los Angeles more than five times over.
questions.source_title: National Hot Dog and Sausage Council - Hot dog consumption statistics

questions.question: What is the fastest dive speed ever recorded for a peregrine falcon, in km/h?
questions.explainer: At 389 km/h a stooping peregrine outpaces a Formula 1 car at full throttle, making it the fastest animal on Earth.

questions.question: How many Boeing 747s were built in total before production ended in 2023?
questions.explainer: Boeing built 1,574 jumbo jets between 1968 and 2023, when the final one, a 747-8 freighter, was delivered to Atlas Air.

questions.question: How many novel drugs did the US FDA's Center for Drug Evaluation and Research approve in 2023?
questions.explainer: That made 2023 one of the busiest years on record for brand-new medicines; 2022 saw only 37 approvals.
questions.source_title: Novel Drug Approvals for 2023 (US Food and Drug Administration)

questions.question: How many keys are on a standard full-size US PC keyboard, including the number pad?
questions.explainer: The US ANSI full-size layout has 104 keys: 26 letters, 10 digits, 12 function keys, the number pad, plus modifiers and navigation keys. The European ISO layout has 105.

questions.question: How many different people flew to the Moon on Apollo missions (1968-72), including those who never landed on it?
questions.explainer: Twelve walked on the surface and twelve more stayed aboard the command module; three of them (Lovell, Young and Cernan) made the trip twice, on Apollo 8, 10, 11-17.

questions.question: How many transistors were on the Intel 4004, the first commercial microprocessor, released in 1971?
questions.explainer: A flagship smartphone chip today has close to 20 billion transistors, roughly 8 million times more: five decades of Moore's law in a single comparison.

questions.question: What was the population of the United States in its first census, in 1790?
questions.explainer: The first census counted 3,929,214 people, about the same as the population of the city of Los Angeles today. Virginia was the most populous state and nearly one in five residents was enslaved.

questions.question: What is the total value of the NBA's 11-year media-rights deals with Disney, NBC and Amazon starting in 2025-26, in US$?
questions.explainer: About US$6.9 billion per season, nearly triple the previous deal. NBC alone pays around US$2.5 billion a year, and TNT lost the NBA after almost four decades.
questions.source_title: NBA: New 11-year media rights deal with Disney, NBC and Amazon worth $76B (Indianapolis Business Journal)

questions.question: What was the measured HPL score (Rmax) of El Capitan, the fastest supercomputer on the November 2024 TOP500 list?
questions.explainer: 1,742 petaflops is 1.742 quintillion floating-point calculations per second, delivered by about 11 million CPU and GPU cores at Lawrence Livermore National Laboratory in California.

questions.question: What was the advertised jackpot of the record US Powerball lottery draw won in California in November 2022?
questions.explainer: That is the annuity value; the lump-sum option was $997.6 million before tax. The jackpot had rolled over for three months at odds of 1 in 292 million.
questions.source_title: Powerball.com - Ticket in California wins world record $2.04 billion Powerball jackpot

questions.question: How many milligrams of caffeine are in a standard 8 oz (240 ml) cup of brewed coffee, per the Mayo Clinic?
questions.explainer: A single shot of espresso has about 64 mg, and the US FDA considers up to 400 mg a day safe for most healthy adults, so about four cups of drip coffee.
questions.source_title: Mayo Clinic - Caffeine content for coffee, tea, soda and more

questions.question: How many people watched Super Bowl LIX (February 2025) on average, according to Nielsen?
questions.explainer: At the time a record for any US telecast, roughly 38% of the entire US population. The audience peaked at 137.7 million in the second quarter.
questions.source_title: Super Bowl LIX makes TV history with over 127 million viewers (Nielsen)

questions.question: How many litres of beer were brewed worldwide in 2023, according to the BarthHaas hop report?
questions.explainer: That is 1.88 billion hectolitres, around 23 litres for every person alive; China, the United States and Brazil are the three biggest brewing nations.

questions.question: How many tonnes of wheat were harvested worldwide in the 2023/24 season?
questions.explainer: That works out to almost 100 kg of wheat for every person on Earth; China, India, Russia and the EU together grow about 60% of it.
questions.source_title: USDA Foreign Agricultural Service - Grain: World Markets and Trade

questions.question: What valuation did SpaceX's December 2024 share sale give the company, in US dollars?
questions.explainer: The $350 billion secondary sale at $185 a share made SpaceX the world's most valuable private company, up from $210 billion just six months earlier.
questions.source_title: SpaceX valuation surges to $350 billion as company buys back stock (CNBC via NBC New York)

questions.question: How much did the Hubble Space Telescope weigh at its launch in 1990, in kilograms?
questions.explainer: Hubble weighed 11,110 kg at launch, roughly the mass of two adult African elephants, and gained about 1,000 kg of new instruments over five servicing missions.

questions.question: What is the area of Australia's Great Barrier Reef, in square kilometres?
questions.explainer: About 344,400 sq km, larger than Italy and visible from orbit, it is the biggest structure on Earth built by living things.

questions.question: How many centimetres can the fastest-growing bamboo grow in a single day, per Guinness World Records?
questions.explainer: Some bamboo species shoot up 91 cm in 24 hours, nearly 4 cm every hour, so you can see the difference between breakfast and dinner.
questions.source_title: Fastest growing plant - Guinness World Records

questions.question: How many individual ants are estimated to live on Earth, per the 2022 study in PNAS?
questions.explainer: About 20 quadrillion, 2.5 million ants for every human, and together they outweigh all wild birds and mammals combined.
questions.source_title: The abundance, biomass, and distribution of ants on Earth - PNAS (Schultheiss et al. 2022)

questions.question: How many standard 20-foot containers (TEU) can the world's largest container ship, MSC Irina, carry, as of 2024?
questions.explainer: MSC Irina and her sister ships are rated at 24,346 TEU; laid end to end, that many twenty-foot boxes would stretch about 150 km.
questions.source_title: List of largest container ships - Wikipedia

questions.question: What was the advertised price of the cheapest Ford Model T, the two-seat Runabout, in the United States in 1925?
questions.explainer: That was the lowest price ever for a new mass-market car in the US, roughly $4,700 in today's money. The same Runabout had cost around $900 in 1910.
questions.source_title: Humboldt State University Special Collections - Price of a Ford (1925 listing)

questions.question: How many joules of energy are released by the complete fission of 1 kilogram of uranium-235?
questions.explainer: One kilogram of fully fissioned U-235 yields about 82 terajoules, roughly 23 million kWh, the same energy as burning around 2,700 tonnes of coal.

questions.question: What was the UK National Living Wage per hour for workers aged 21 and over from April 2024?
questions.explainer: The 9.8% rise from £10.42 was the largest cash increase ever, and the age threshold dropped from 23 to 21. A 37.5-hour week at this rate pays about £430.
questions.source_title: Business Wales - National Minimum Wage and National Living Wage rates 2024

questions.question: How many years ago, as of 2026, was the Rosetta Stone carved?
questions.explainer: The stone records a decree issued in 196 BC under Ptolemy V. Its three scripts let scholars finally decipher Egyptian hieroglyphs in 1822.

questions.question: How many servings of instant noodles were eaten worldwide in 2023, according to the World Instant Noodles Association?
questions.explainer: China and Hong Kong alone account for about 42 billion servings; worldwide it works out to roughly 15 packets per person per year.
questions.source_title: World Instant Noodles Association - Global demand for instant noodles

questions.question: How many optical sensors (DOMs) are frozen into the Antarctic ice at the IceCube Neutrino Observatory?
questions.explainer: IceCube's 5,160 digital optical modules hang on 86 strings between 1,450 and 2,450 metres deep, turning a cubic kilometre of South Pole ice into a neutrino telescope.

questions.question: How much play money is in the bank of a standard US Monopoly set (2008 edition onward)?
questions.explainer: 30 bills of each of the seven denominations from $1 to $500. Each player starts with only $1,500, so most of the cash stays in the bank. Pre-2008 sets held $15,140.

questions.question: How many Muslims were there in the world in 2020?
questions.explainer: Muslims were about a quarter of humanity in 2020 and the fastest-growing major religious group; Indonesia, Pakistan and India have the largest Muslim populations.
questions.source_title: Pew Research Center – How the Global Religious Landscape Changed from 2010 to 2020

questions.question: How long is the Trans-Alaska Pipeline, from Prudhoe Bay to the port of Valdez, in km?
questions.explainer: The pipeline runs 1,288 km (800 miles) from the Arctic coast to Valdez; about half of it is raised on supports so the warm oil does not thaw the permafrost beneath.

questions.question: How fast was the Parker Solar Probe moving at its record closest approach to the Sun in December 2024, in km/h?
questions.explainer: On 24 December 2024 Parker passed 6.1 million km from the Sun at 192 km per second (430,000 mph), fast enough to cross the USA in about 20 seconds.
questions.source_title: Closest approach to the Sun by a spacecraft (Guinness World Records)

questions.question: How many hot dogs and buns did Joey Chestnut eat in 10 minutes to set the Nathan's Famous Fourth of July contest record in 2021?
questions.explainer: That is one hot dog every eight seconds for ten minutes; at a 2024 exhibition against Takeru Kobayashi he pushed the all-time mark to 83.

questions.question: How deep is the Challenger Deep, the deepest point of the Mariana Trench?
questions.explainer: If Mount Everest were dropped into the Challenger Deep, its summit would still be more than 2 km underwater.

questions.question: How many copies of Minecraft had been sold across all platforms when Mojang announced its milestone in October 2023?
questions.explainer: That makes Minecraft the best-selling video game of all time, well ahead of Grand Theft Auto V; the previous official count was 238 million in 2021.

questions.question: According to the IAEA, how many nuclear power reactors were in operation worldwide at the end of 2024?
questions.explainer: The IAEA counted 417 operating reactors with a combined capacity of about 377 GW at the end of 2024; counting Japanese units in long-term suspension pushes the figure to around 440.
questions.source_title: Nuclear Power Reactors in the World, 2025 Edition - IAEA

questions.question: How many minutes did the longest professional tennis match ever (Isner v Mahut, Wimbledon 2010) last?
questions.explainer: 11 hours 5 minutes spread over three days. The fifth set alone finished 70–68 and took 8 h 11 min, longer than any other complete match in history.
questions.source_title: Isner–Mahut match at the 2010 Wimbledon Championships (Wikipedia)

questions.question: How many kilometres away is Proxima Centauri, the nearest star to the Sun?
questions.explainer: At 4.25 light-years, about 40 trillion km, Proxima is 1,600 times farther than Voyager 1 has travelled in nearly 50 years.

questions.question: How much did the Manhattan Project cost in total, in 1945 US dollars?
questions.explainer: The project cost nearly $2 billion in 1940s money, about $27 billion today, and employed over 130,000 people at its peak. Around 90% of the cost went to building factories and producing fissile material, not to the bombs themselves.

questions.question: On an average day in 2023, how many babies were born worldwide?
questions.explainer: That is about 132 million births a year, or roughly 250 every minute, against about 61 million deaths.

questions.question: How much did the United States pay Russia for Alaska in 1867?
questions.explainer: About two cents an acre for 586,000 square miles, roughly $130 million in today's dollars. Critics mocked the deal as 'Seward's Folly'.

questions.question: How many days does a human red blood cell circulate before it is broken down and recycled?
questions.explainer: Your bone marrow makes about 2 million new red blood cells every second to keep the supply of roughly 25 trillion steady.

questions.question: How many years did Louis XIV reign as King of France?
questions.explainer: The Sun King ruled from May 1643 to September 1715, 72 years and 110 days, the longest verified reign of any sovereign monarch in history. He outlived his son and grandson.

questions.question: Roughly how many lumens of light does a standard 60-watt incandescent light bulb give out?
questions.explainer: A classic 60 W bulb produces about 800 lumens, which is why LED bulbs sold as '60 W equivalent' are rated at 800 lumens while drawing only 8 to 10 watts.
questions.source_title: Lumens and the Lighting Facts Label - U.S. Department of Energy

questions.question: How many bricks were used to build the Empire State Building?
questions.explainer: The 102-storey tower also used about 57,000 tons (roughly 52,000 tonnes) of structural steel and went up in just 410 days. Ten million bricks would build around 1,000 ordinary houses.

questions.question: How many merchant ships of 100 gross tons or more made up the world's commercial fleet in January 2023?
questions.explainer: UNCTAD counted 105,493 commercial ships of 100 gross tons and above at the start of 2023; bulk carriers, tankers and container ships provide most of the carrying capacity.

questions.question: How many wild mountain gorillas were there in 2018, combining the latest Virunga and Bwindi census counts?
questions.explainer: All of them live in just two forest regions of central Africa; the total combines the 2015-16 Virunga count (604) and the 2018 Bwindi-Sarambwe count (459), up from around 600 in the early 1980s.

questions.question: What plasma temperature, in degrees Celsius, is the ITER fusion reactor designed to reach?
questions.explainer: ITER aims for 150 million °C, about ten times hotter than the core of the Sun, because without the Sun's crushing gravity fusion needs far higher temperatures to work.

questions.question: How many fire hydrants are there on the streets of New York City?
questions.explainer: That is roughly one hydrant every 100 metres along the city's 6,000-plus miles of streets, all fed by the water mains DEP maintains.
questions.source_title: NYC Department of Environmental Protection: Fire Hydrants

questions.question: How many minutes per day did the average American aged 15 and over spend watching TV in 2023?
questions.explainer: About 2.6 hours a day, which is more than half of all leisure time. Socialising and communicating, by comparison, gets roughly 35 minutes a day.
questions.source_title: U.S. Bureau of Labor Statistics: American Time Use Survey - 2023 Results

questions.question: How tall is Michelangelo's marble statue of David, not counting its pedestal?
questions.explainer: At 5.17 metres, David is about three times the height of an adult man. It stood outdoors in Florence's Piazza della Signoria for 369 years before moving indoors in 1873.

questions.question: What was the launch price of the original Apple Macintosh (128K) in the United States in January 1984?
questions.explainer: That is roughly US$7,700 in 2025 dollars; Apple had planned to sell it for $1,995 but raised the price by $500 to help pay for the launch marketing, including the famous '1984' commercial.

questions.question: How many Pokémon trading cards had been produced worldwide in total by the end of March 2024?
questions.explainer: About eight cards for every person on Earth. Almost 12 billion of them were printed in that single fiscal year alone.

questions.question: At what temperature in kelvin does liquid nitrogen boil at normal atmospheric pressure?
questions.explainer: Liquid nitrogen boils at about 77 K, which is -196 °C: cold enough to shatter a rose, yet still some 75 degrees warmer than the LHC's superconducting magnets at 1.9 K.

questions.question: As of 2025, how many years has Madrid's Sobrino de Botín been open, counting from the founding year Guinness World Records recognises?
questions.explainer: Guinness World Records dates Botín to 1725 and lists it as the oldest restaurant in continuous operation; it marked its 300th anniversary in 2025, though historians note the current business opened under the Botín name in 1865 and the 1725 date rests partly on tradition.
questions.source_title: Restaurante Botín - History and evolution of Botín (Guinness World Records: oldest restaurant)

questions.question: What record price in US dollars did a single bottle of 1945 Romanée-Conti wine fetch at Sotheby's in New York in 2018?
questions.explainer: Only about 600 bottles of the 1945 vintage were made before the old vines were pulled out and replanted. The 2018 sale set the auction record for a single bottle of wine; the very same bottle was resold at Acker in March 2026 for US$812,500, the new record.

questions.question: What was the GDP of Tuvalu, the Pacific island nation of about 10,000 people, in 2023, in current US dollars (World Bank)?
questions.explainer: One of the smallest economies on Earth, smaller than many single shopping malls. A notable slice of its income comes from leasing its '.tv' internet domain and selling fishing licences.
